transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date/Time: 2026-10-12 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Priya Shah (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Aisha Gomez (BlueWave Platform Eng), Tom Rivera (Head of ML), Leah Chen (Security)

Summary: quick gate-check for onboarding sprint, access handoffs, early perf numbers, and security signoffs. Focus on access gaps: SSO, VPC peering, KMS, and a longer benchmark for tail latencies. Action items captured at end.

Topics: onboarding status, credentials & gateway, staging perf, KV/prefix cache behavior, SSO/KMS, SOC2 evidence request, timeline to pilot cutover.

----- Transcript -----
[00:00:00] Priya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick check in today, we'll run through access gate items and then Marcus will walk the perf plan. Um, if we can keep to 45 minutes that'd be great.
[00:00:15] Aisha: great thanks Priya, I have a hard stop at 14:40 UTC but hopefully that fits.
[00:00:25] Tom: same, quick note, we got the initial sandbox creds friday and we did a smoke test. small things with the gateway token rotation but otherwise ok.
[00:00:40] Marcus: yeah and that smoke test looked fine on our end, we saw successful handshake to Redwood Dedicated endpoint, though I think it tripped on the kv cache when sequences >2k.
[00:01:05] Leah: can you repeat kv cache? we logged something in the security log that might be related to token refresh.
[00:01:15] Marcus: sure, so prefix/KV cache — sometimes the runtime will evict partial cache entries for long contexts, there was a brief spike in recompute which bumped tail latencies up to 1.1s for a 2k token prefix in the sandbox. could be the batcher config.
[00:01:40] Aisha: ok that aligns with our observations, we saw bursts on the gateway around 13:12 UTC yesterday.
[00:01:50] Priya: good, action there is Marcus will run a longer bench with more realistic chat traces, 10k tokens and mixed batch sizes. can you confirm cadence Marcus?
[00:01:58] Marcus: yep I'll run it today and tomorrow, and post results in the sheet, looking at p50/p95/p99 and also the cost per 1k tokens estimate.
[00:02:20] Tom: we really need the p99 tail because our product surface has some synchronous paths where 800ms vs 1.8s is noticeable.
[00:02:30] Marcus: totally, will include tail metrics and breakouts by sequence length.
[00:02:40] Leah: quick security question — for KMS, are you supporting customer-managed keys in the private/pvt deployment? our compliance requires bring-your-own-key or HSM.
[00:02:55] Priya: yes for Private deployments we support KMS and can integrate with your cloud KMS or an HSM via our KMS bridge. small caveat is we need the KMS key ARN and a service account to grant decrypt for the inference nodes.
[00:03:15] Leah: and will Redwood's control plane ever see plaintext model outputs? we need to record that for SOC2.
[00:03:25] Marcus: no, in Private mode the control plane only sees telemetry and health, payloads can be routed directly on-prem or via VPC peering. that said, in Hosted we do process responses. i'll send an architecture note.
[00:03:40] Aisha: we prefer VPC peering so logs don't transit public internet.
[00:03:48] Priya: noted. Aisha, can you confirm the VPC CIDR and preferred peering window?
[00:03:55] Aisha: i'll share the CIDR and the ops windows for next week by Friday.
[00:04:05] Tom: on SSO — we tried the SAML flow in staging, it failed at assertion due to audience mismatch. guess config issue.
[00:04:15] Priya: okay we'll double-check the ACS URL mapping; i'll send the SAML mapping doc.
[00:04:25] Leah: also need RBAC mapping for service accounts to limit access to dev vs prod models.
[00:04:35] Marcus: we have role mappings in the console, but the mapping for machine-to-machine isn't always obvious in the UI. i'll walk through a sample policy in the doc.
[00:04:50] Priya: another security ask — SOC2 evidence, Leah mentioned, is Redwood able to share the iso audit or SOC2 artifacts?
[00:04:58] Marcus: we can share our SOC2 Type II summary and a standard security pack; for detailed artifacts we'll raise an NDA scoping if needed.
[00:05:10] Leah: that works, we have a 3rd party auditor doing a readiness check so a summary is fine for now.
[00:05:20] Priya: Great. moving back to infra readiness — Aisha, last week you mentioned a firewall rule that blocked outbound egress to certain IP ranges, is that still pending?
[00:05:32] Aisha: yes firewall team needs the exact egress list. can you provide IP ranges, or are you on DNS endpoints?
[00:05:40] Marcus: we publish both, but for the pilot we recommend using DNS plus one static egress range for the gateway; i'll paste the recommended list in the sheet.
[00:05:55] Tom: one nuance — in our HIPAA flow we need to ensure logs are suppressed for PHI. is there a redact setting?
[00:06:05] Marcus: yes we have token level redaction and can avoid storing raw outputs in the control plane for Private. we'll include config options.
[00:06:15] Aisha: perfect.
[00:06:20] Priya: ok let's talk timeline — what's realistic for cutover to pilot traffic if access and perf check out?
[00:06:28] Tom: if all access is green and perf is within p95 target (<=600ms), we can pilot with limited traffic in two weeks. but if p99 is high we may need to extend.
[00:06:40] Priya: note on p95 target — that was customer-defined, but we can play with batching and quant profiles. Marcus, any quick wins?
[00:06:50] Marcus: turning on prefix caching and reducing quant to int8 for the model variant we use gave us 15-20% latency decrease in our internal runs; but cost tradeoffs apply. also smarter batching windows help.
[00:07:08] Leah: is quantization allowed by our security policy?
[00:07:15] Tom: yes, model fidelity tests needed but our unit tests guard for hallucination delta.
[00:07:24] Aisha: on fidelity, we need to run our prompt set through Redwood Optimize recommendations to ensure no regressions.
[00:07:33] Marcus: we can run a small eval harness against your prompt set if you provide it, or you can anonymize prompts. we'll respect PHI constraints.
[00:07:45] Aisha: we'll scrub PHI and share 200 representative prompts.
[00:07:50] Priya: excellent. next, credentials handoff — we noticed token rotation occurs every 12 hours in sandbox, what's the recommended production cadence?
[00:08:00] Marcus: production token TTL typically 24h with short-lived service certs for nodes. for long running streams we use refresh tokens in the client. i'll include examples.
[00:08:15] Tom: any known gotchas with streaming and refresh? last time we saw a mid-stream reconnect.
[00:08:22] Marcus: that's usually due to ephemeral TLS renegotiation on the gateway; we'll tune keepalive and also recommend client-side retry logic with idempotency keys.
[00:08:35] Priya: we'll add that to the runbook.
[00:08:40] Aisha: small note — our ops team wants a health endpoint for the gateway that maps to our alerting. do you expose metrics via prometheus?
[00:08:50] Marcus: yes Prometheus metrics and a /healthz endpoint are available in Private . in Hosted we expose metrics through a metrics stream.
[00:09:02] Leah: please flag which metrics contain potential PII so we can vet them.
[00:09:08] Marcus: will do.
[00:09:12] Priya: ok I'm going to read back the key action items. Marcus to run the 10k token perf bench and post p50/p95/p99 + sequence breakout by Oct 18. Priya to send SSO/SAML mapping doc and the security pack by Oct 14. BlueWave (Aisha) to share VPC CIDR and egress window by Oct 15. Leah to confirm KMS/HSM preference. Anything to add?
[00:09:40] Tom: also include the redaction config and a sample RBAC mapping for service accounts.
[00:09:48] Marcus: yep will include both.
[00:09:55] Aisha: will do.
[00:10:00] Priya: cool. other blockers?
[00:10:05] Aisha: just internal firewall and one pair of creds for the staging run, otherwise we're on track.
[00:10:12] Tom: safety note — we want to run a micro rollback test when we flip pilot traffic, so fallback and circuit breaker patterns need validation.
[00:10:22] Marcus: Redwood has a canary and automatic fallback to a smaller model variant; we'll walk through playbook during the next ops rehearsal.
[00:10:33] Leah: and we'll want to see audit logs for that switch.
[00:10:38] Priya: yes audit logs are retained — we'll share retention windows and log schema.
[00:10:45] Marcus: quick Q from me — do you want us to provision temporary dedicated capacity for the initial pilot or use hosted pool with burst?
[00:10:55] Tom: for cost reasons we'd prefer hosted burst initially but we might reserve dedicated if throughput needs spike.
[00:11:05] Priya: we can start hosted with a reserved burst cushion and then convert if steady-state. I'll include cost estimates.
[00:11:12] Aisha: send the billing model so finance can sign off.
[00:11:17] Priya: will do.
[00:11:20] Marcus: ok last technical note: we'll instrument kv cache hit rates and prefix reuse metrics in the next run so you can correlate ops spikes.
[00:11:32] Aisha: that's helpful.
[00:11:36] Priya: wrap up — let's schedule the next sync for 2026-10-19 same time unless you prefer earlier after the bench runs.
[00:11:45] Tom: 10-19 works.
[00:11:48] Leah: works for me.
[00:11:50] Priya: perfect thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links to the sheet, SAML doc, and the security pack.
[00:12:00] (crosstalk, small goodbyes)

--- End of meeting ---
